question.problem:
To improve the paint's grip on the wall surface, Mike must dissolve $6.5$ grams of a particular additive in each liter of paint. How much additive is needed if Mike plans to use $2.5$ liters of paint?

shared_context.problem: Mike needs to paint some walls. Each wall has an area of ${(\frac{17}{4})}^{2}$ square meters.

earlier_parts.problem:

${\text{m}}^{2}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The exact area of  ​each wall is ${(\frac{17}{4})}^{2}\,{\text{m}}^{2}.$

Writing ${(\frac{17}{4})}^{2}$ with multiplication signs, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{17}{4})}^{2} & ={{\frac{17}{4}\times \frac{17}{4}}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}} \\  & =\frac{17\times 17}{4\times 4} \\  & =\frac{289}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{17}{4})}^{2}=\frac{289}{16}.
$$
